verdict.tagline: Stunning turn-based combat wrapped in a demanding, sprawling journey.
for_you_if: you love deep turn-based combat with active timing
you enjoy intricate storytelling that rewards patience
you want a challenging journey through a dense world
not_for_you_if: you need stable performance on handheld hardware
you struggle with strict reaction-based parrying mechanics
you dislike complex narratives with overwhelming opening hours

claims.claim: The game encounters severe performance and compatibility problems on the Steam Deck, requiring major graphical adjustments or leading to crashes.

Game crash  everytime after proloog on steamdeck

This game seems SO good. I don't often leave reviews, but I just wanted to say that if you are planning on playing it, play it on something other than the Steam deck. Getting even "medium" graphics settings takes major tinkering, and makes the FPS drop down to ~25. I'm usually the person who doesn't care about this sort of thing (I'll play competitive shooters with potato graphics and ~40 FPS), but this game really requires timing for parries AND an understanding of the characters' emotion. Maybe it will be enough for some people, but I decided to refund and hold out until I got a better system. Great game. Recommend if you have a better rig. But make sure to really think about it before you get it on Steam Deck.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks a mini-map, which makes it easy to get lost while exploring.

citations.review_text: So far, so good. I'm only a little over 3 hours in and for an indie dev company, this game is fantastic.  However, I feel like maybe another year of development may have helped.  There's a few QOL quirks.  For one, there's no mini map and its pretty easy to get turned around while exploring. There's a Parry/Dodge system that is also a bit quirky.  A quick time option would have been nice. Also, the lip sync is TERRIBLE, like 1970's Chinese Kung Fu Chinese/English Dub Movies Terrible.  The graphics are the true stand out here, in my opinion. Its beautiful.  The overall aesthetic of the game is awesome.  I like the story so far, the characters are good and I'm already captivated.  I'll update this as I play more, but these are my initial thoughts.

the world design is absolutely magestic, full of colors that easily stand out. the effects are marvellous, absolutely exceeded my expectations. the combat feels very smooth and very different from traditional turn based combat, and i love it for that reason (im a very dedicated hater of regular turn based combat). the only downside to it is that the world is so vast that its very easy to get lost in certain areas, especially since you have no map for most of the time you spend navigating, but other than that i have nothing to criticize, i see why it won goty, and well deserved at that

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as combining turn-based mechanics with real-time dodging and parrying inputs.

citations.review_text:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 — my honest take
Not a turn-based JRPG guy at all, but this game got me. Didn't expect that.
The combat's the reason — it's turn-based but you're actually dodging and parrying in real time, so it never feels like you're just clicking through menus. Add insane art direction (Belle Époque France but make it dreamlike), a soundtrack that goes from haunting orchestra to full metal without ever feeling wrong, and characters who actually talk and act like real people — and yeah, I lost track of time more than once.
Moments that had me glued to the screen:

The expedition setting off, and the game telling you upfront who's not making it back
First look at the Paintress — beautiful and genuinely unsettling at the same time
Walking into a brand new area for the first time and just letting the visuals do the talking
Boss fight finishers — slow-mo cinematic kills after a hard-fought battle, feels like a movie
Each character's big backstory reveal — earned, not filler
The story twists between acts that recontextualize everything you thought you knew
The final act — you'll want to just sit there after the credits roll

Definitely worth it. Don't think twice — grab it when it's on sale.

Beautiful visuals and interesting turn based mechanics.  Not just tactical, because you do need to still use timing for jumps, evades, and etc.   This is a unique gaming experience that should not be missed.

citations.review_text: This game is amazing. Reminds me a little of the Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order and Survivor games crossed with Baldur's Gate. But the storyline is just wow. One thing I would change (other than parrying seeming a bit glitchy) is can the devs please reduce the number of "yay you killed the boss! Wait, no you didn't, got to do it once more!" incidents... it gets a little tedious. But super minor complaint in the face of an epic game.
Amazing game and story. Parry window is too tight for my likely though.

I bought this game on steam after already playing it on a different platform, so it's safe to say that I like it.

I'll keep this review spoiler-free as much as possible, so...
Overall the story is great and the game looks amazing with a lot of interesting areas to explore. 

I enjoyed the combat but I can see how some people might not. The parry/qte system does require you to learn a lot of different enemy combo attacks, and it's not always clear exactly when you need to parry, so you'll probably fail a lot before getting it right. I would say however, that while I did like the combat, I don't think that this is the type of game you play [i]for[/i] the combat. 

I've seen a bunch of reviews mention the third act, and I do agree that it's the weakest part, but it's still good. The main difference is that this part opens up the entire world to exploring as you want, and most of the content is additional to the main story - in contrast to the previous acts that's more linear and you come across areas & side quests in a way that makes sense to the main story.

So many people I know told me this game brought them joy, so I really did want to like this and share that with them. But I just don't. I tried my best to temper my expectations for this game after it swept TGA last year. I was sure it would be at least good, regardless of how overhyped it may or may not be. I was determined to give it a fair shot. And yet, I simply could not bring myself to enjoy Expedition 33.

It's not an awful game by any means and there are plenty of positives. Narratively it's mostly fine, it's a story about grief, how it blinds us, the trials and tribulations it brings and the lengths people go to avoid confronting reality, that sort of thing. The actual execution of it is nothing I would sing praises to the heavens for but I think it's okay, the idea is good, even with the clumsy pacing and sometimes strangely written dialogue. The music is also great, I found myself humming the main Lumière motif while doing chores. The voice actors also did a great job, Jennifer English in particular is standout and Andy Serkis is great as usual. If this had been a film or series it'd be pretty good.

But for me that's about as far as the positives go. For the rest of it, I really, [i]really[/i] do not see what people find so compelling about it. I think Team Cherry (Hollow Knight devs) summed it up best when they described it as "broadly palatable." 

My biggest grievance by far is with combat. Dodging was fine, although the parry timing felt really strange to get used to even with the clear audio cues. But the window/timing of them wasn't my issue with it. I think dodges and parries [i]can[/i] work in a turn-based system, but in this game I simply do not think it works at all. For me, the critical issues are:

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players master the demanding mechanics and dense storytelling despite structural hurdles late in the game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that platforming elements can feel clunky or poorly executed.

citations.review_text:
Things I like:
. Extraordinary worldbuilding
. Breathtaking visuals and art style
. Memorable, likeable characters
. Interesting, gripping story (only Mass Effect 2 can hold a candle to it)
. Voice actors suck you right into the world
. Dialogue doesn't get boring
. First game that made me genuinely both laugh and cry
. Soundtrack is simply perfect (varied and harmonious)
. Many different and interesting weapons
. OP- builds in endgame
. Vast passive skill tree, if you spend time collecting the pictos (I loved trying new builds)
. Leveldesign is stunning and doesn't get repetitive
. Turn- based combat (even the QTEs and heavy parrying focus)
. Numerous enemy types
. Intuitive main and combat menus
. Accessible achievements
. Super ultrawide support
. Satisfying ending with a meaningful choice (even though with a sad or dark subtext)

Things I do not like:
. If you do the endgame content in advance, the game gets way too easy
. The map is a bit unclear (if you zoom out, the names of the locations disappear too early)
. Platforming is clunky sometimes
it's a great story based game with a unique fighting system but it's a bad platformer.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe Act 3 as causing a sharp spike in difficulty and leaving players feeling lost or lacking direction.

citations.review_text:
Very confused by this game. It started strong with the story and all the mysteries around the characters, and then act 3 happened and it all fell flat. you start wandering around, no clue where to go, you either enter a place where you're overpowered and one shot everyone or you're in a really difficult place where fights take too much time. I picked the game after having played sekiro and was looking for some parry based mechanic game and this one is not it. while sekiro's parry is reactive, you see the attack coming and you react to it, this one has what I would call "predictive parrying", you meet a boss, and there is no way you'd win from first try, attacks tempo is too randomized with either an absurd speed or some feints that break the rhythm, the parry window is also too small. you have to die multiple times while learning his attacks patterns, and then start parrying knowing in advance what every attack is like, and at that moment you realize you know all the attacks the fight stops being challenging.
Add to that some glitch added lately where the game would crash if using DX12 when going to the continent. lot of posts online on it, some said to switch to dx11, only solution I found was switching dlss to ultra performance before going out to the continent otherwise it's a guaranteed crash.

While I loved the game from the beginning, my first try in 2025 ended at Act 3 when the structure of the game changes drastically. I felt completely lost and the difficulty spiked massively.

The second time playing, a year later, I was loving the game again but dreaded the coming act 3. This time I sought some advice on how to tackle the act 3 and was able to enjoy the rest of the game and finally finish it.

While the act 3 is problematic, this game is still a masterpiece. The story, writing, acting, music, visuals and gameplay are all top notch.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the turn-based combat relies heavily on active timing inputs like parrying and dodging rather than traditional passive stats.

citations.review_text:
This game exudes a universal tale that can be enjoyed by anyone. The experience throughout my playthrough gave me waves of nostalgia for a Final Fantasy title I never played. Game mechanics are fun, easy to understand, and there are a million or more different ways to customize your build for your style of play.

I would recommend this game to anyone that can hold a controller. Difficulty is optional, but rewarding.

No game is perfect. As a turn-based combat fan, I was disappointed that this game was advertised as such. Strategy and stats did not matter as much as my manual dexterity and ability to time inputs. However, this slight messaging error did not hamper my ability to enjoy an otherwise delightful game.

Soundtrack, visuals, gameplay, story, and characters are all magnificent. 10/10 would play through New Game+. Right after I beat this last boss....

I don't usually write reviews but... This game is beyond amazing. The journey had me hooked from start to end, and it literally makes me sad to think I will never get to experience it for the first time again. First of all the game looks beautiful, and each area is uniquely captivating and makes you want to explore as you go. Not once did I wish I could fly or fast travel. The music is absolutely phenomenal, and the voice acting is possibly the best of any game I have ever played. The story was interesting and full of surprises, as were almost all of the characters no matter how small a part they played. The combat was awesome, they really managed to make "turn based" fun and challenging with the parry/block/jump feature. 10/10 hands down, a true masterpiece and only half of the price of other games now days! If you like rpgs even a little bit then you should just buy it, seriously the music alone is well worth the $40 lol I promise you

-Short (<30 hours) game if you just want the main story

-Great Story
-Beautiful Graphics
-BANGER MUSIC (one of the best in any video game ever - I still listen to the OST frequently while at work)

I'm sure everyone else has said what you need to know about this game. This is also the Game of the Year in 2025. (If you haven't played it yet, why haven't you?)

TIs time. This game is just absolutely phenomenal. I personally believe that it deserves all the awards it swept, simply because it's that good. The combat is kind of familiar with dodges, parries, and even the idea of turns, yet it is so refreshing and new. The gameplay is so smooth and instinctive, yet it is very punishing and unforgiving. The story is creative and captivating. It is so beautiful, and the way they tell it only makes it better and better. You can very easily get lost in this world, meeting goofy NPCs, finding hidden merchants, or even killing a random thug level enemy that gives you the craziest upgrade to your loadout. I have no words to describe the music; my favorite was the gestrals. The characters are all well designed and unique; they all have their own personalities, emotions, and troubles. And I can't not mention the cinematics, They are simply the cherry on top. There are challenging parts of the game, but you shouldn't let them scare you from trying, for it will prevent you from experiencing all of the above. The game has many choices for difficulty settings, letting people with all types of skill levels have their own fun in the world of Lumiere. I just recently defeated Simon the Divergent, so I felt like it was time to share my feelings on this game. If I have anything to say, it's that the bosses of the endless tower are simply ridiculous and mostly aren't even a fun challenge, except Simon the Divergent, as even though I spent weeks learning and perfecting his pattern, I had fun and liked the boss. In summary, just the main story without any additional content is worth experiencing, but everything else adds so much.

claims.claim: Reviewers find that the opening prologue is heavy on dialogue and can feel dense, overwhelming, or tedious before opening up at Act 1.

citations.review_text:
[h2]Endure until Act I. It is absolutely worth it.[/h2]
The only real exception to how extraordinary this game is lies in its opening. You are immediately thrown into an unfamiliar world, surrounded by characters discussing events, concepts, and people you know nothing about yet. It can feel like the beginning of a dense HBO series, with an overwhelming amount of information introduced all at once.

At the same time, this approach gives the world a remarkable sense of depth and authenticity. It feels as though this place existed long before the player arrived, with its own history, relationships, and conflicts already in motion. Still, because the prologue is heavily focused on dialogue, it can initially be somewhat difficult or tedious to engage with. But please, endure until Act I. It is absolutely worth it.

Expedition 33 is an undeniable masterpiece. Its story is deeply involving and unfolds with the confidence and precision of a beautifully directed film. The characters grow throughout the journey, and so does your emotional connection to them. The plot combines a profound mystery with an exciting and often unpredictable adventure.

The visuals are stunning, not merely because of their technical quality, but because of the game’s extraordinary art direction(no pun intended). Its environments, character designs, colors, and imagery feel genuinely otherworldly.

The gameplay is challenging, satisfying, and consistently engaging. Its systems demand attention and skill without losing their sense of fun. The soundtrack is also one of the finest I have heard in a very long time. I am certain it will remain with me long after finishing the game, possibly for the rest of my life. It deserves to stand alongside the most memorable and accomplished video game soundtracks, such as those of The Legend of Zelda and Portal.

Ultimately, Expedition 33 is a masterpiece filled with depth, symbolism, and countless layers of meaning. It makes extensive use of metaphor a…

I'll be honest, I came into this game not expecting to like it and after finishing it, it's now in my top 10 games of all time. 

It really took me a few hours of play time before I was able to grasp everything but by the end of Act 1 I could really see the vision. This story is not a happy one and at times it deals with some really heavy topics so just be prepared for that. 

By the end of the game all of the characters grew on me and I really enjoyed the way each character could provide something in a fight. I will say, the Pictos and Lumina system is a little overwhelming at times but learn it quick and you'll have such a better time getting through the fights in this game. 

The story can be really confusing at times...however...making sure to talk to each character while at camp will help to clear some things up. The character and world building in the game is a bit slow but just talk to everyone and you will eventually understand most things. 

The music and art...some of the best I've ever seen/heard in gaming. I played with a good pair of headphones most of the time and was blown away by the beautiful music they included. It really just makes the game so much better. 

Overall, I give the entire game a 10/10. I put about 70 hours into this playthrough and still haven't seen or collected everything. I'm sure I will come back to it again to 100% it.

I'll be honest, I came into this game not expecting to like it and after finishing it, it's now in my top 10 games of all time. 

It really took me a few hours of play time before I was able to grasp everything but by the end of Act 1 I could really see the vision. This story is not a happy one and at times it deals with some really heavy topics so just be prepared for that. 

By the end of the game all of the characters grew on me and I really enjoyed the way each character could provide something in a fight. I will say, the Pictos and Lumina system is a little overwhelming at times but learn it quick and you'll have such a better time getting through the fights in this game. 

The story can be really confusing at times...however...making sure to talk to each character while at camp will help to clear some things up. The character and world building in the game is a bit slow but just talk to everyone and you will eventually understand most things. 

The music and art...some of the best I've ever seen/heard in gaming. I played with a good pair of headphones most of the time and was blown away by the beautiful music they included. It really just makes the game so much better. 

Overall, I give the entire game a 10/10. I put about 70 hours into this playthrough and still haven't seen or collected everything. I'm sure I will come back to it again to 100% it.
